goal: Finish the migration-framework follow-up, produce a clean release, deploy it safely to the current EC2 Compose production authority, verify it end to end, reconcile records, and clean only proven-disposable artifacts.
scope: All current and future repository work items; completed work is retained only as dependency evidence.
source_of_truth: work-items.ndjson is the materialized baseline and work-item-events.ndjson is the append-only journal for every new task and update. Reconcile both with scripts/work_items.py or work-items.sql. GitHub issues and PRs own defect-specific requirements and discussion; repository runbooks own procedures; this registry references rather than copies them.

rule: References such as #765 and PR#766 resolve through these templates.
Read the current revision before executing a task. Do not duplicate or weaken these sources here; if they conflict, stop and ask the human.

rules: One frozen PR review cycle produces at most one aggregate follow-up issue containing deduplicated actionable findings and exact source-thread links.
Search open and recently closed issues and PRs by source URL, component, and failure mode before creating an issue; link an existing issue when it already covers the finding.
Split only a private security disclosure or a genuinely independent release blocker with separate ownership.
Creating or updating the aggregate issue ends automatic activity. It never authorizes a worktree, implementation, PR, merge, deployment, or another review cycle.
Automatic implementation depth is zero; every new implementation cycle and every exact-head merge requires explicit human authorization.

P0/P1 security, data-integrity, startup, default-path, or production-contract regressions block merge and production unless the human explicitly resolves or waives them. P2/P3 findings block only when they invalidate the promised contract.
Do not manufacture work to keep agents active.
replaces_for_remaining_scope: work-plan.md review rule requiring one issue per actionable comment
any inference that a follow-up issue authorizes implementation

reason: The human paused recursive development and production work after the review-follow-up loop was identified.
unlock: Explicit human authorization naming the next task or implementation cycle.
prohibits: code or documentation edits beyond this requested plan

repository_status: untracked work-plan.md before this plan was created
dynamic_state_rule: Refresh GitHub, origin/main, worktree cleanliness, live production, and check status before relying on this snapshot.

completed_non_issue_todos: clean previously confirmed-merged worktrees and branches
verify prior issues, PRs, docs, and cleanup
create the future EC2-to-EKS migration tracker #725
rule: Do not reopen or reimplement completed work unless a current task has direct contrary evidence.

reason: The prior todo marked the work complete, but GitHub still reports the issue open.

decision: Do not merge or deploy PR#766 while #767 is unresolved or unwaived.

title: Eliminate conflicting local execution instructions
actions: Treat this NDJSON file as the only remaining execution queue.
Inspect untracked work-plan.md; preserve any still-useful canonical links by reference, then delete it or reduce it to a pointer to this file.
Confirm no agent prompt template still says one issue per actionable comment or automatically starts follow-up implementation.
acceptance: Exactly one local execution queue governs remaining work.
The bounded aggregate-review policy is unambiguous.
No tracked or untracked plan can restart recursive work without human authorization.

title: Resolve #765 and the P1 restart regression #767 as one authorized implementation cycle
preferred_path: Keep PR#766 frozen as reviewed evidence; do not merge it.
From refreshed origin/main, create one clean replacement branch/worktree only after explicit authorization.

Implement the combined acceptance contracts from #765 and #767 without creating another issue: fresh zero-row SQLite auto-safe startup must drive required safe jobs to validated before serving, and an already-validated SQLite store containing later usage must restart without rerunning or invalidating the immutable migration.
Preserve manual and deployment-job behavior, bounded checkpoint/resume idempotency, safe failure diagnostics, and fail-closed handling of genuine migration or validation errors.

Add deterministic regressions for fresh zero-row startup, validated nonempty restart, and a real failure path; run focused tests, relevant SQLite and disposable PostgreSQL coverage where shared code is affected, full Go tests, vet, docs/package checks when contract wording changes, and a changed-path smoke.
Open one replacement PR linked to both issues; complete the ten-minute unchanged-head review. Aggregate all new actionable comments into one deduplicated follow-up issue and stop.

Obtain explicit authorization for the exact replacement head into main; after merge verification, close or supersede PR#766 with a link to the replacement and close #765/#767 only when their acceptance evidence is recorded.
acceptance: Fresh auto-safe SQLite startup serves only after required jobs validate.
A validated SQLite store with accrued usage restarts successfully without replaying immutable migration work.
Manual and deployment-job contracts remain unchanged.
All required checks pass on the exact merged head.
No recursive implementation cycle starts from review feedback.
rollback: No reverse migration. Revert code only before production migration; after a restore-required migration, follow the release-specific database restore contract in docs/DATA_MIGRATIONS.md.

title: Reconcile issue and worktree state before release
actions: Confirm #732 acceptance is fully represented by merged PR#733 and its evidence; close #732 with a concise link if authorized, otherwise record the exact remaining criterion without creating another issue.

For the issue-702 worktree, note that #702 is closed while PR#711 is closed unmerged and its branch is not proven merged. Compare its commits/patch to origin/main and issue closure evidence; remove it only if clean and fully represented or explicitly abandoned by the human.
After the #765/#767 replacement is merged or explicitly abandoned, remove the clean issue-765 worktree and obsolete local branch only when no unique work remains.
Prune only stale worktree metadata created by confirmed removals.
acceptance: Every retained worktree has an open purpose.
No unique unmerged work is deleted.
GitHub issue states match verified delivery state.

title: Create a clean, reviewable release candidate from current main
actions: Fetch origin and fast-forward the clean local main; do not package the stale snapshot recorded above.
Confirm #765 and #767 are closed by merged evidence or explicitly waived, PR#766 is resolved, required checks on all merged heads passed, and no P0/P1 release blocker remains.
Run rtk make release-notes-from-git, review generated language for customer safety and migration/rollback accuracy, update required version metadata and upgrade guidance, then run docs QA/build.

If release-note or generated-doc changes exist, commit them on a focused branch, open one PR, observe it for ten minutes under policy.bounded_review_followup, and obtain exact-head merge authorization.
Refresh main again and require a clean tree and a stable non-dirty git-described version.
acceptance: Release notes describe the migration contract, operator impact, caller impact, validation, and restore-required rollback without private deployment facts.
Main is clean, current with origin/main, and contains every authorized fix and generated artifact.
No unresolved P0/P1 finding or unreviewed source change is in the candidate.

title: Run complete local release validation
actions: Run focused migration and SQLite auto-safe regressions before the broad suites.
Run the changed-path router-migrate plan/apply/resume/verify/status smoke against local disposable SQLite and PostgreSQL as required by docs/DATA_MIGRATIONS.md.
Run applicable production-derived fixtures under testdata/smokes/production-derived without production secrets.
Investigate every failure; do not label a failing suite irrelevant without recording a reproducible reason and passing the narrower release-critical suite.
acceptance: Focused regressions, release-critical Go suites, vet, docs QA/build, admin browser E2E, package validator self-test, diff check, and migration smoke pass on the same clean candidate SHA.
evidence: Sanitized command, exit status, named contract, environment class, and safe scalar results only.

title: Build and validate Docker release artifacts
actions: From the clean committed candidate, run rtk make package-docker to build linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 Docker packages.
Verify package-content validation, architecture, embedded docs/admin assets, image tags, build timestamp, version, and absence of private production markers or secret/state files.
Record SHA-256 checksums and identify the linux/amd64 package for the current production host.
Load and smoke the packaged image locally when Docker is available; assert /version matches the candidate and the binary architecture.
acceptance: Both architecture packages pass content validation.
The selected amd64 artifact checksum, version, commit, build timestamp, and image tag are recorded.
The release artifact is built from a clean non-dirty commit.
evidence: Artifact names, checksums, sizes, version metadata, and validator results; never package env.json, config.production.yaml, tokens, private keys, license payloads, logs, DBs, or dist source residue.

title: Capture production baseline and approve rollback prerequisites
actions: Verify live /readyz, /version, authenticated /v1/models, metrics-admin access, ordinary-caller metrics rejection, representative usage report, compose service state, host architecture, disk capacity, and current image before changing anything.
Confirm the EC2 Compose endpoint remains production authority and EKS remains staging-only; #725 owns any future cutover and is out of this rollout.
Verify ignored config.production.yaml is synchronized with the live config by checksum without printing either config; validate YAML structurally.

Run the new package's non-serving migration status/plan against the production database using protected runtime inputs and capture only safe scalar migration IDs, compatibility, pending counts, required jobs, and rollback class.

Create a timestamped package/runtime backup and an approved pre-migration database backup because migration 2026080501 is restore-required; verify backup completion and record protected references without exposing paths or credentials.
Define go/no-go owners, maintenance window, traffic drain, rollback trigger, and maximum outage before stopping the old service.
acceptance: Baseline is healthy or deviations are explicitly resolved.
Package and database rollback artifacts are verified before migration.
The migration plan is compatible with the candidate and contains no unknown ID/digest.
A human gives explicit production go authorization after reviewing the safe preflight summary.
rollback: Before migration, restore the previous package/runtime backup. After migration begins, never reverse migrate; restore the approved database backup and previous package together when the release contract requires rollback.

title: Install the package and complete the non-serving production migration
actions: Upload only the selected amd64 package, verify its checksum on the host, unpack into a fresh deployment directory, copy forward only approved live compose config/state/logs/.env/token files from the timestamped backup, set the exact SMART_LLMROUTER_VERSION, load the packaged image, and validate docker compose config.
Drain/stop the serving router before maintenance. Do not start the new serving process until migration completion is proven.

Execute the canonical non-serving sequence from docs/DATA_MIGRATIONS.md using protected DSN environment and container entrypoint controls: plan → confirm approved backup → apply → resume every required data job checkpoint → verify → status → serve.

Use status after each resume to select the next checkpoint ordinal. One resume performs one bounded checkpoint; never assume ordinal 0 completes historical-usage-validation-v1 or any job with more rows than one checkpoint.
Require every release-defined bound data job to be validated and the ledger current/compatible before deployment-job startup.

On any pending/running/paused/cancelled/failed/unknown job, digest mismatch, timeout, lock loss, or verification failure, keep serving stopped and execute the approved rollback or recovery decision; do not bypass the gate.
acceptance: Migration 2026080501 and all required data jobs are validated.
Final verify and status succeed with safe current/compatible state.
No serving process ran against a partially migrated or unvalidated ledger.
No reverse migration, raw SQL, raw data, DSN, credentials, or unrestricted output is used as evidence.
evidence: Sanitized plan/apply/checkpoint/verify/status summaries, checkpoint ordinals, aggregate rows scanned/updated/skipped/failed, durations, and backup evidence reference class.

title: Start and verify production containers
actions: Start the reviewed Compose deployment, inspect router container state and bounded logs, and require stable readiness.
Verify /readyz and /version return 200 and exactly match the packaged version, commit, build timestamp, Go version, and linux/amd64 architecture.
Verify the serving migration policy accepts the validated ledger and no startup loop, database write failure, license failure, or migration-status warning appears.
If readiness or version is wrong, stop and use the approved package-plus-database rollback path.
acceptance: Compose reports the intended router healthy.
Public readiness and version identify the exact deployed artifact.
The router remains stable through the agreed observation interval.

title: Run production API, telemetry, report, and real CLI acceptance
actions: Run bounded authenticated OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, and Anthropic Messages text smokes against a deployment-defined permitted group; retain only safe request IDs, status, latency bucket, selected target metadata, usage presence, and sanitized error class.
Run tool-call and streaming-usage smokes appropriate to current production routes; assert tool-call shape, real created-file contents, and required usage chunks.

Run actual Codex CLI text/tool smoke through Responses and actual Claude Code text/tool smoke through Anthropic Messages using the documented router auth precedence; assert output/result metadata and file contents.
Verify /metrics succeeds only for metrics_admin and returns 403 metrics-forbidden to an ordinary caller; verify aggregate migration metrics are present without tenant/token labels.
Verify the read-only admin migration report and representative usage reports on production PostgreSQL, including latency/performance views, without exposing raw rows.

For any reproducible non-2xx, schema mismatch, translation loss, malformed tool call, missing usage, or dialect discrepancy, stop rollout and follow AGENTS.md incident-fixture/issue policy; aggregate same-cycle findings under policy.bounded_review_followup.
acceptance: All three API skins, required tool/stream surfaces, both real CLIs, metrics isolation, migration visibility, and usage reporting pass.
No raw prompts, tool schemas, images, outputs, tokens, hashes, keys, credentials, config, DSNs, or raw database rows are retained.
evidence: Sanitized endpoint/dialect, model group, HTTP status, request ID, latency bucket, tool/usage assertions, selected target metadata, report name, and aggregate outcome.

title: Verify embedded production documentation
actions: Verify /docs/ and the required migration, upgrade, deployment, API compatibility, errors, model access, usage reporting, VLM/tool, release index, release note, and upgrade-guide pages return 200.
Confirm every sampled page banner and docs-version metadata match /version and the deployed build timestamp.
Confirm public pages contain no source-control workflow language, private host/path/SSH details, secrets, production configuration, or stale pre-migration guidance.
Exercise public examples that changed in this release using placeholder credentials or approved ignored runtime credentials as required by AGENTS.md.
acceptance: Hosted docs are reachable, version-aligned, current, customer-safe, and consistent with the shipped migration and rollback behavior.

title: Reconcile production snapshot, release evidence, and deployment notes
actions: Confirm local ignored config.production.yaml and live config checksums match without displaying contents.

Update deployment.md with deployed package/image tag, source commit, build timestamp, migration IDs/job completion summary, intentional backup reference, health/API/CLI/docs/report evidence, rollback boundary, and cleanup performed.
Post concise sanitized completion evidence to the active delivery issues/PR or designated rollout tracker; do not reopen closed issues merely to duplicate deployment.md.
If deployment.md changes, commit it in a focused post-deployment PR, observe review under policy.bounded_review_followup, and obtain exact-head merge authorization.
Post a Google Chat rollout announcement only through configured runtime webhook values and only as required by the authorized communication plan; never print or persist webhook URLs.
acceptance: Repository deployment ledger and live artifact agree on version and state.
Evidence is sufficient to reproduce the safety conclusion without secrets or duplicate narrative.
Any post-deployment PR is merged or explicitly left as the sole documented outstanding record.

title: Clean production and local deployment artifacts
actions: After production is healthy, remove uploaded package/config staging files, superseded temporary unpack directories, and stale Docker images/build cache/containers; retain only intentional timestamped backups required by rollback policy.

Remove generated local release artifacts only when no longer needed for evidence or rollback; never add dist, logs, DBs, env.json, config.production.yaml, tokens, license material, or state files to Git.

Remove clean confirmed-merged or explicitly abandoned worktrees/branches identified by task.reconcile_tracking; do not delete PR#766 or issue-702 artifacts until their unique-work checks and human decisions are complete.
Prune worktree metadata and verify the remaining worktree inventory, branch purposes, repository status, open PRs, and open scoped issues.
acceptance: Production has no unnecessary uploaded package or temporary deployment residue.
Every remaining backup is intentional and documented.
Every remaining local worktree/branch maps to active authorized work.
The repository is clean except for explicitly retained ignored operational files and this tracked plan.

title: Produce the final completion record
actions: Recheck #732, #765, #767, PR#766, any replacement/release/deployment-note PRs, required checks, and exact merge commits.
Recheck live readiness/version, migration verified state, production smokes, hosted docs, config checksum parity, deployment.md, backups, and cleanup.
Report completed items, exact evidence, intentionally open future work such as #725, and any waived risk. Do not create new work from informational observations.
acceptance: All tasks in this plan are complete or explicitly waived by the human with rationale.
No unrecorded P0/P1 risk, dirty worktree, orphaned branch, unmerged required PR, stale production note, or deployment residue remains.
The human receives one concise final record with links rather than duplicated issue content.

parallelism: Only production_smokes and hosted_docs may run concurrently after start_and_health. All other critical-path tasks are sequential because each consumes the prior task's immutable evidence.

requirements: The active SQLite migration defects are resolved or explicitly waived; no P1 blocker is merged or deployed.
The release candidate is clean, fully validated, packaged for both supported architectures, and traceable to one commit.
Production migration follows plan → approved backup → apply → all required data jobs validated → verify → status → serve.
Production health, API skins, tools/streaming, real CLIs, metrics isolation, reports, and hosted docs pass.
Config snapshot, deployment ledger, GitHub state, backups, and cleanup are reconciled.
Review feedback cannot recursively start implementation; one aggregate issue per cycle and explicit human authorization remain enforced.
